hello.note: Reply: wa-uh-LAY-koom us-suh-LAAM. سلام alone is casual.

good_morning.note: Literally 'morning's greeting'; the salaam covers the day too.

goodbye.note: 'God keep you'; shared with Urdu and Sindhi's other neighbors.

how_are_you.note: Polite/plural 'you'; casual singular is tuun KAY-in aa-HEEN.

no_problem.note: Literally 'no matter/thing'; brushes off a small favor.

please.note: Literally 'doing a kindness'; the everyday word for please.

excuse_me.note: Literally 'listen'; polite plural form, to get attention.

sorry.note: 'Please forgive (me)'; مون کي افسوس آهي is wordier, 'I regret'.

of_course.note: Emphatic yes; يقينن (yuh-QEE-nun, 'certainly') is a synonym.

amazing.note: 'Astonishing'; a Persian-rooted word shared with Urdu.

cheers.note: 'Stay happy'; a toast-like well-wish, not a clinking custom.
